newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: World solar summit debates plans behind doors.
newsitem.headline: World solar summit debates plans behind doors.

text.p: Delegates to a world solar summit went into closed session on Tuesday to debate an ambitious plan to provide energy to those without electricity by the middle of the next century.

The two-day conference, due to end later on Tuesday, won resounding pledges of political support when it opened, but some delegates were unhappy over a lack of concrete financial commitments to realise their vision.

About 300 solar and other renewable energy projects were presented at the summit under a long-term United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organistion (UNESCO) programme aiming to provide power to 2.4 billion people living without electricity.

The summit -- attended by delegates, including 12 heads of state and governments, from 100 countries -- emphasised there was a need to convince the world that solar, wind, geothermal and other renewable sources of energy were generally cheaper, environmentally friendly and more easily accessible than other sources.
